abstract: We establish an asymptotic form of Sun's conjecture concerning representations by the ternary quadratic polynomial \[ P(x,y,z)=x(5x+1)+\dfrac{y(5y+1)}{2}+\dfrac{z(5z+1)}{2}. \] More precisely, we prove that every sufficiently large integer is represented by $P$, with an effectively computable threshold. The proof begins by reducing the representation problem to that of a positive definite ternary quadratic form. We then study its genus and associated theta series, using explicit representation identities to determine the Shimura lift of the relevant weight-$3/2$ cusp form. Through Waldspurger's formula, this allows us to relate its Fourier coefficients to central values of quadratic twists of a weight-two modular form. Finally, effective lower bounds for class numbers, together with subconvexity estimates, show that the cuspidal contribution is dominated by the genus average for all sufficiently large integers, yielding the desired result.

title: Critical Well-Posedness of a Euler-Chemotaxis System in 2D
abstract:
This article is about well-posedness results for a 2D Euler-Chemotaxis-Consumption system with initial data in scale critical spaces, namely existence, uniqueness and critical initial data to solution continuity. This problem is related to the well-known family of Keller-Segel equations, although it bears major differences which will be crucial for our study.
  In most recent results, solutions to such Chemotaxis-Consumption systems have used a free-energy balance law to obtain well-posedness. This has the disadvantage of requiring initial data to be positive almost everywhere. Our main goal, in addition to sharp well-posedness, is to show that this positivity condition is not needed for existence and uniqueness. In fact, we will never use the concept of free-energy in our proof.
  Our argument revolves around an understanding of the scaling of the different parts of the equation, and especially the subcritical interaction terms. This will allow us to upgrade basic low regularity estimates (e.g. mass conservation) into critical bounds. In the process, we find out that closing $L^2$ estimates leads to the Besov space $\dot B^0_{\infty, 2}$ as the most natural choice of regularity for the initial chemo-attractant concentration. Extensive use of real interpolation also plays a key role for deriving Chemin-Lerner bounds for the solutions.

title: A new notion of Dirichlet boundary condition for elliptic equation of divergence form
abstract:
In this paper, we consider Dirichlet boundary conditions for elliptic equations in divergence form on rough domains by introducing a truncation-based weak solution framework that circumvents global Sobolev trace obstacles. We establish well-posedness on bounded admissible domains for continuous boundary data and $L^2$
  sources, deriving boundary Hölder regularities that require only uniform ellipticity and an exterior measure-density condition. This approach eliminates the uniform domain regularity and coefficient continuity imnposed in Guam, Wang and Zhou(2026). Furthermore, on sufficiently flat Reifenberg domains, we obtain boundary $C^α$ regularity for any $α\in (0,1) $ using natural energy estimates, thereby bypassing
  $L^p$($p>\frac {n}{2}$) restrictions found in Lian and Zhang(2026). Crucially, we obtain global $H^1$
  regularity for Hölder boundary data ($α>\frac 12$) a posteriori, without requiring small-BMO coefficient assumptions on the coefficients.

title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory for Lines and Finite Configurations
abstract: A classical question in Euclidean Ramsey theory, posed by Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus, asks which finite configurations $X\subset\mathbb E^2$ must appear in blue under every red--blue coloring of the plane having no red pair of points distance one apart. For $m \ge 2$, let $\ell_m$ denote the line of $m$ points with consecutive points distance one apart. Tsaturian showed that $\ell_5$ is unavoidable; we improve this to $\ell_7$. Additionally, we show that in every three-coloring of the plane in which two colors contain no $\ell_2$, the third color must contain an $\ell_3$. To conclude our discussion on lines, we prove several related results on two-colorings of higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces where both colors avoid longer lines. Our methods also extend to other point configurations. In any two-coloring of the plane in which one color contains no $\ell_2$, we show that the other color must contain both a regular pentagon of side length one and a unit square together with its center. We also prove that every two-coloring of three-dimensional space contains either a monochromatic unit square or a monochromatic noncoplanar tetrahedron with four edges of length one and two of length $\sqrt{2}$. Our proofs combine Székely's averaging inequalities for distance-avoiding sets with the Fourier-analytic and linear-programming methods of de Oliveira Filho and Vallentin, together with a theorem on rotation-invariant measures from OpenAI's recent work on the Hadwiger-Nelson problem.

title: Non-closed products in branch and weakly branch groups
abstract: We prove that the first Grigorchuk group and the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group are not double coset separable, disproving a conjecture of Grigorchuk, Leemann and Nagnibeda. More generally, every finitely generated regular branch group with bounded activity contains two finitely generated, profinitely closed subgroups with trivial intersection whose product is not closed. Every infinite finitely generated subgroup of the first Grigorchuk group or the Gupta-Sidki $3$-group also fails to be double coset separable. We extend the construction to the $p$-Basilica groups and, using polynomial activity, to the long-range group, whose derived subgroup we prove to be finitely generated. Under an additional hypothesis on finite quotients, we determine the closure of the product. Membership in the constructed product is decidable in the first Grigorchuk group.

title: Discrete-Time Stochastic Control Beyond i.i.d. Noise
abstract: We study discrete-time stochastic control problems where the noise driving the state dynamics is a stationary infinite-order chain rather than an i.i.d. sequence. We formulate the problem as a controlled Markov process by enlarging the state space to include the posterior distribution of the noise given the state-action history. Assuming that the sensitivity of the noise transition kernel to past noise values decays exponentially, we show that the expected total variation distance between the full-history and finite-memory noise filters decays at rate $\sqrt{N}ρ^{\sqrt{N}}$. We use this result to construct finite-memory control models and establish explicit near-optimality bounds for their policies. Finally, under suitable ergodicity conditions, we show that Q-learning converges to the optimal solution of the approximate model, so the same performance bounds apply to the learned policies.

title: On Algebraic LNE models of complex affine algebraic curves
abstract: We give a sufficient condition for an affine complex curve to have an algebraic complex LNE model.

title: Scattering of water waves in presence of a partially immersed obstacle
abstract: We study linear water waves in two dimensions in a fluid of infinite depth containing a fixed, partially immersed obstacle. Under natural geometric assumptions on the wetted boundary, we construct the harmonic lifting and prove that the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator is an unbounded, self-adjoint and non-negative operator on a $L^2$ space. This yields global well-posedness and conservation of energy. We establish the absence of trapped modes and, by a compact perturbation argument, a limiting absorption principle at every positive spectral parameter. Consequently, for all finite energy initial data, the physical local energy tends to zero as $|t|\to\infty$, including in neighborhoods of the obstacle and the contact points. Quantitative resolvent estimates and fractional regularity in the spectral parameter yield algebraic local energy decay for Sobolev initial data in weighted $L^2$ spaces.

title: Mesoscopic derivation of predator-prey dynamics via diffusive fast-reaction asymptotics: cross-diffusion and fear effects
abstract: We propose a kinetic derivation of a spatial predator-prey model with cross-diffusion interactions and a Beddington-DeAngelis functional response. At the mesoscopic level, we divide the two populations into distinct behavioral states: prey can be active or hidden in a refuge, while predators can be either searching or handling. The microscopic state of each subpopulation is described in terms of group size and a continuous directional velocity variable, with state transitions governed by suitable Boltzmann-type interaction operators. By combining a diffusive scaling with a slow-fast formulation of the kinetic reaction operators, we formally derive a macroscopic reaction-cross-diffusion system for the total population densities of prey and predators. The limiting model consistently recovers the Beddington-DeAngelis functional response along with its associated nonlinear diffusion terms. Crucially, the kinetic upscaling yields a predator-dependent prey growth term taking a logistic form with an effective carrying capacity. This carrying capacity depends non-monotonically on predator density because prey redistribute between active and refuge states. Since density-dependent competition acts separately within these behavioral states, intermediate predator levels reduce aggregate crowding and thereby increase the effective carrying capacity of the total prey population. Overall, our derivation provides a mechanistic link connecting predator-induced behavioral shifts, refuge use, and macroscopic cross-diffusion.

title: An Accelerated Dynamic Stochastic Primal-Dual Method for Multi-stage Stochastic Optimization
abstract: We consider multi-stage stochastic optimization problems with smooth convex stage costs and linear linking constraints. Dynamic stochastic approximation (DSA), a stochastic first-order method, uses a recursive structure whose memory requirement grows only linearly with the number of stages. Its implementation, however, requires an exact solution of the proximal subproblem associated with the stage cost, and this subproblem often admits no closed-form solution. To resolve this issue, we develop an accelerated dynamic stochastic primal-dual (A-DSPD) framework that retains the recursive value-function structure and only requires the gradient of the stage cost. Within this framework, each stagewise saddle-point subproblem is solved by an inexact accelerated stochastic primal-dual method (iASPD), which applies Nesterov acceleration to the smooth stage cost and uses recursively generated stochastic $ε$-subgradients for the nonsmooth downstream value function. For the stochastic composite saddle-point problem, after $N$ primal-dual updates, iASPD yields optimality and feasibility bounds in which the contribution of the smooth stage cost decays at a faster rate $O(1/N^2)$, while the terms associated with stochastic $ε$-subgradients of the nonsmooth value function decay as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$, up to the prescribed oracle inexactness. We also develop bounds for the stochastic $ε$-subgradient estimators and the dual iterates, which yield complexity guarantees for A-DSPD. Specifically, A-DSPD computes an $ε$-solution using $O(1/ε^4)$ sampled scenarios and $O(1/ε^5)$ primal-dual updates for three-stage problems. We further extend the method and its convergence analysis to problems with an arbitrary finite number of stages. Numerical experiments on three-stage stochastic portfolio models illustrate the empirical advantage of the proposed method.

title: A resolution of the Erdős similarity problem in the large
abstract: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. This resolves the Erdős similarity problem in the large.

title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
abstract: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.

title: Sharp Proximity Bounds for Integer Programs with Few Rows
abstract: We study the proximity between an optimal vertex of a standard form linear program with constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ and an optimal integer solution. When $m = 2$, we prove the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ-1$, where $Δ$ is the largest absolute maximal minor of $A$. When $m = 1$, we express the difference between an optimal LP vertex and an optimal integer solution as a nonnegative combination of certain generators in the kernel of $A$ with a bounded coefficient sum. This implies sharp proximity bounds for all norms when $m=1$. Combining this representation with its known counterpart for Hilbert bases due to Sissokho, we develop techniques that transfer results from $m=1$ to $m=2$. Along the way, for $m=2$, we prove that such a representation exists for an extended Gomory group relaxation and obtain the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ$ for Graver basis elements. We also present a new short proof of Sissokho's result and lower bounds on the proximity for all $m$ and $Δ$.

title: Complete self-shrinkers with scalar curvature bounded below
abstract: Let $X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm of the second fundamental form. We prove that up to an orthogonal transformation, the image $X(M^n)$ is a sphere $S^n(\sqrt n)$, or a hyperplane $\mathbb R^n$ or a generalized cylinder $ S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{n-k},\ 1\le k\le n-1$ if scalar curvature $R$ satisfies $R\geq -3/2$, which improves the recent results in \cite{CLW1}.

title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
abstract: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
abstract:
We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second iterate is sufficient for the arboreal Galois representation to be surjective. We also discuss experimental evidence suggesting that a similar statement involving the fourth iterate may hold in general.
  The results were obtained in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic's AI model); they are also formalized in Lean (except for the experimental evidence).

title: High degree covers and genericity
abstract:
It is known that the genuine irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations of a tame $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne cover of a $p$-adic split connected reductive group are all generic, when the degree $n$ is suitably large. This has been established by studying the the structure of the Gelfand-Graev representation as a module under the action of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra.
  In this paper, we present a different proof based on metaplectic Moy-Prasad theory.

title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
abstract: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.

title: Congruences for Dedekind numbers
abstract: We study congruence properties of Dedekind numbers $d_n$. Our approach relies on actions of $p$-subgroups of symmetric groups on posets of monotone functions and leads to the congruences $d_{10}\equiv 106\pmod{210}$, $d_{11}\equiv 117\pmod{210}$, and $d_{12}\equiv 12\pmod{30}$. In particular, $d_{11}$ is odd, confirming a claim stated by Yamamoto without a proof.

title: Weak Quasi-Convexity: First- and Second-Order Conditions, Monotonicity, and Quadratic Functions
abstract: In this paper we introduce weakly quasi-convex functions, which are a generalization of weakly convex functions. We study the behavior of weakly quasi-convex functions in Euclidean spaces. We provide several illustrative examples that demonstrate the scope and distinctive features of this new class of generalized convex functions. We derive a necessary condition for weak quasi-convexity under certain assumptions and provide an example showing that its converse is not true for discontinuous functions. Under the continuity assumption on the function involved, a sufficient condition is provided with an adjusted weak quasi-convexity modulus. Also, we bring out various kinds of monotonicity in connection with weakly quasi-convex functions through the gradient mapping. We provide several illustrative examples that interpret and emphasize the newly introduced notions. We establish a first-order necessary condition for the class of differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. Conversely, we show that a differentiable function satisfying this first-order condition is weakly quasi-convex with an adjusted modulus. We provide a second-order necessary condition under appropriate assumptions using second-order Dini derivatives. As a consequence, we derive a Hessian-based necessary condition for the class of twice continuously differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. We provide an example to show that the converse of the second-order characterization does not hold. Furthermore, we establish various kinds of necessary conditions concerning general quadratic functions and provide many counterexamples for the failure of their sufficiency. Finally, we derive several consequences of weak quasi-convexity for optimization problems.

title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
abstract: This work summarizes some updates to the ropelength problem, concerning the shortest possible contour length of a unit-thickness knot, that were derived with the assistance of ChatGPT-5.6 Luna. The first of two main results is that the universal lower bound for a knot with crossing number C has been improved from $L\geq1.105C^{3/4}$ to $L\geq2.0996C^{3/4}$, achieved by further separating local and global terms in an optimization integral. The second main result is a bound relating ropelength to stick number (s), such that $L\geqπ(s-1)$. This implies stronger lower bounds for the ropelengths of at least 41 torus knots, and a specific class of pretzel knots. Other results include an improved packing-based lower bound for T(Q,Q) links and an optimized standard parameterization for torus knots. There were many problems for which the LLM was unable to render assistance, for example in reducing the numerical coefficients or scalings of known universal upper bounds.

title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $ω_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.

title: The exponent $3/4$ for the exceptional sets of the equations $K/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$
abstract: For $K\ge4$ let $E_K(N)$ be the number of integers $2\le n\le N$ for which $K/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$ has no solution in positive integers; $K=4$ is the Erdős-Straus equation. We prove that $E_K(N)\le N\exp(-c((\log N)^3/K)^{1/4})$ with absolute constants $c,B>0$, uniformly for $4\le K\le(\log N)^3/B$. This improves the exponent $2/3$ of Vaughan's bound of 1970. The bound is non-trivial for $K$ up to a constant times $(\log N)^3$, which is, up to a factor $(\log\log N)^{2+o(1)}$, the scale at which, by work of Pomerance and Weingartner, exceptional primes become common. The sieve is combinatorial: a truncated inclusion-exclusion over the classes of parametric solutions, whose second moment is the partition function of a two-copy polymer gas, bounded by a real form of the Kotecký-Preiss criterion. Averaging over the residue classes of the small primes gives the family its full mass, and summing each cluster in a random order bounds the cluster sums. Since a divisor of an exception is an exception, nothing about the small primes themselves is needed, and the sieve can use the classes of the whole family of parametric solutions, one triple per class. All constants are explicit, and the whole proof has been checked in the proof assistant Lean 4.

title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the incompressible porous medium equation on the whole plane
abstract: We study the asymptotic stability of the steady state $e_s(x)=-x_2$ of the incompressible porous media equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For every $s>2$, we prove that sufficiently small initial perturbations $θ_0\in H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ of $e_s$ generate unique global solutions $ρ=e_s+θ$, where $θ$ remains uniformly bounded in $H^s$ and converges strongly to zero in $H^s$ as $t\to\infty$. The main innovations of this work are threefold. First, exploiting the structure of the equation, we construct a weighted energy that eliminates the need to control $\|\nabla u^2\|_{L^1_tL^\infty_x}$. Second, rather than estimating the anisotropic commutators directly, we study the integral terms containing these commutators and establish suitable bounds through refined computations in frequency space. Third, we establish convergence in the highest-order $H^s$ norm under uniform energy bounds involving only an $L^\infty_tH^s_x$ bound on $θ$ and an $L^2_tH^s_x$ bound on $\mathcal R_1θ$.

title: A generalized Vojta-Rémond inequality over adelic curves
abstract: We extend Dill's generalized Vojta-Rémond inequality to proper adelic curves of characteristic zero, under an explicit Siegel hypothesis. The geometric case is closely related to recent work on Mordell-Lang plus geometric Bogomolov for semi-abelian varieties. Our formulation retains Dill's generality for products of distinct projective varieties. The appendix establishes the Siegel input for arithmetic function fields with nef and big polarizations on the model.

title: Thom Morphisms, Self-Intersection, and the Sectional Category of a Section
abstract: For sections between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we compare module sectional category, sectional category and relative category after rationalization. Fibre Poincaré duality turns the compatibility of derived evaluation with the section into a derived self-intersection formula. We prove equality of the three invariants under any of four hypotheses: a base-dimension bound, finite total rational homotopy of the fibre, a smooth section with closed manifold fibre, or a compatible relative Frobenius model. Projective bundles over CP^k with fibre CP^r have common value k + r, which is unbounded even for fixed fibre. Whether fibre Poincaré duality alone suffices remains open.

title: A Kato-Type Criterion for Vanishing Viscosity and Magnetic Diffusivity Limits for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the vanishing viscosity and magnetic diffusivity limits for the compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Under the assumptions of interior regularity and uniform local boundedness near the boundary, we establish a Kato-type criterion under which finite energy weak solutions to the dissipative MHD system converge to weak solutions to the ideal MHD system as the viscosity and magnetic resistivity coefficients decrease to zero. In particular, under such criterion, the anomalous energy dissipation in the vanishing viscosity and diffusivity limits for MHD is precluded.

title: Invariant measures, Gelfand pairs and integral representations
abstract:
We prove that whenever a Gelfand pair acts cocompactly on a locally compact space, there is a measure relatively invariant under a "parabolic" subgroup. That result seems new even for simple Lie groups, in which case it admits a much more direct proof.
  Along the way, we obtain for general Gelfand pairs a variant of Furstenberg's invariant ray theorem for minimal parabolics. We use this to establish an integral representation theorem for positive spherical functions in complete generality, extending the Harish-Chandra representation. A similar representation theorem is given for positive harmonic functions.

title: Representations of the quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
abstract: Let $q$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity with $p\ge2$, and let $H=D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ be the Drinfeld double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the dual Hopf algebra and the cross relations of $H$. A change of generator gives a classification of the simple $H$-modules. Their isomorphism classes are indexed by $\mathbb Z_{2p}^{\,2}$. We construct their projective covers, compute their dimensions, and determine which simple modules are projective. Finally, we prove that $H$ is strictly wild for every $p\ge2$ by constructing a fully faithful exact functor from finite-dimensional $\Bbbk\langle x,y\rangle$-modules to finite-dimensional $H$-modules.

title: Decay rates for monotone operator flows in the space of probability measures
abstract: Motivated by the mean-field dynamics of large populations of interacting agents, we study the long-time behavior of flows driven by monotone demicontinuous operators on the Wasserstein space. For cocoercive operators, we prove that the flow converges to a zero of the operator and that the operator residual and the metric speed decay as $o(t^{-1/2})$, so that the population comes to rest (the agents asymptotically stop moving). We also consider Tikhonov regularized flows of merely monotone demicontinuous operators and show that the operator residual and the metric speed tend to zero, with rate $O(1/t)$ when the Tikhonov parameter is $α/t$ with $α\geq 1$, and that the trajectory converges to the zero of minimal second moment, which is a Dirac mass, so that the agents reach consensus (all agents reach the same point). Finally, we study a discrete analogue for nonexpansive operators and show that the generated sequence converges to the fixed point closest to a reference Dirac mass; this fixed point is again a Dirac mass, so that consensus is also reached under this scheme. The main arguments rely on a specially tailored superposition principle, which represents the flow as a curve in a fixed Hilbert space of random trajectories, where the crucial estimates are derived.

title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
abstract: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.

title: Communication-Learning Co-Design for Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
abstract: Wireless federated learning (FL) suffers from two coupled bottlenecks: statistical heterogeneity across clients and communication-constrained model synchronization over unreliable wireless links. Instead of focusing on algorithmic design and/or wireless resource optimization, this paper provides a systematic study of pinching antenna (PA)-empowered FL for heterogeneous wireless networks and develops a unified communication-and-learning framework. Specifically, we integrate a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) architecture with a heterogeneity-robust FL algorithm based on client variance reduction and dual quantization, so as to jointly mitigate communication bottlenecks and client drift. On this basis, we further develop a two-stage SWAN-assisted downlink protocol and formulate fairness-oriented uplink optimization problems for PA positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization design. Efficient solution frameworks are then derived for the resulting downlink and uplink optimization problems. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed design in convergence speed and final accuracy under non-independent and identically distributed data and communication bottlenecks.

title: Euclidean and Hermitian Self-Orthogonal Codes from Divisible Codes
abstract: Self-orthogonality and divisibility are two fundamental properties of linear codes, and the relationship between them has long been of interest. Huffman and Pless (2003) showed that every binary \(4\)-divisible code is Euclidean self-orthogonal, that a ternary code is Euclidean self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(3\)-divisible, and that a quaternary code is Hermitian self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(2\)-divisible. The general case remained open for a long time. In 2024, Li and Heng settled the odd-characteristic case, proving that every \(p\)-divisible code over \(\F_{p^m}\), with \(p\) odd, that contains the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. In this paper we treat the even-characteristic case: we prove that every \(4\)-divisible code over \(\F_{2^m}\) containing the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. We also prove that, for every prime \(p\), every \(p\)-divisible linear code over \(\F_{q^2}\), where \(q=p^m\), that contains the all-one vector is Hermitian self-orthogonal. These criteria make the construction of self-orthogonal codes from divisible codes simple and efficient. As applications, we recover the known Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonality of generalized Reed--Muller codes and obtain several infinite families of new Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonal codes, which give rise to infinite families of quantum codes with excellent parameters.

title: Rank Reversals in Efficient Vectors for Pairwise Comparisons
abstract: Studied are the orders among alternatives given by efficient vectors for a reciprocal matrix A. The focus is upon: 1) existence of efficient vectors with a given order and 2) discrepancies between the ranking for a pair of alternatives resulting from an efficient vector and from the corresponding entry of A, called rank reversals. We use matrix intervals in which the consistent matrices built from efficient vectors lie. The existence of efficient vectors (or those from constituent convex subsets) with a rank reversal at a given position is characterized. The minimum number of rank reversals for a reciprocal matrix among all weight vectors is described and it is shown that there is an efficient vector that has this number of rank reversals. A way to construct such a vector is given. The order transitive and the uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices are shown to be, respectively, the matrices for which there is an efficient vector with no rank reversals and the matrices for which all efficient vectors have no rank reversals. The effects on rank reversals of addition and deletion of alternatives are also discussed. Using numerical experiments, the frequencies of rank reversals in certain formulaic weight vectors are given.

title: Lengthscale Estimation for the Gaussian Kernel and Deterministic Response Functions
abstract: The uncertainty estimates Gaussian processes output rely on the chosen covariance kernel and its hyperparameters. We study the fixed-domain asymptotics of the maximum likelihood and cross-validation estimators of the lengthscale parameter of the popular infinitely smooth Gaussian kernel when the observations are produced by a fixed univariate response function. No theoretical results for Gaussian lengthscale estimation exist in this setting. We prove lower bounds on the lengthscale estimators that depend on the regularity of the response function, as measured by the rate of decay of its Fourier transform. If the response function lives in the Hilbert space of the Gaussian kernel with lengthscale $\ell$, the lower bounds have a straightforward dependency on $\ell$. For bandlimited functions and functions whose Fourier transforms decay as $\exp(-a \lvert ω\rvert^γ)$ for $a > 0$ and $γ> 2$, we prove that the estimators blow up essentially at least as fast as $(\log n)^{(γ-2)/(2γ)}$ in the number of data points, $n$. Bandlimited functions are identified with $γ= \infty$. Unlike analogous results for finitely smooth Matérn kernels, our results make no assumptions on the geometry of the observation points. Numerical experiments illustrate the results.

title: Global existence and sharp decay rates of weak solutions for the 2D inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress tensor diffusion
abstract: This paper is devoted to the global existence and optimal decay rates of weak solutions to a two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion. For $\frac{1}{2}<β<1$, by virtue of energy estimates and compactness arguments, we establish the existence of global weak solutions with $(u,τ)\in H^{1}\times (H^{1}\cap L^{\infty})$. Moreover, based on the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory and the improved Fourier splitting method, we derive the optimal decay rates. In particular, by constructing a suitable low-frequency energy functional and exploiting the dissipation mechanism of the coupled system, we obtain the optimal $L^\infty$ decay rate for the stress tensor.

title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface
abstract: We study rational points of bounded maximum-coordinate height on the split four-nodal Cayley cubic surface over \(\mathbb Q\), with its nine lines removed. Writing \(U\) for this open subset and \(N_U(B)\) for its counting function, we establish \[ N_U(B)\sim c_{\mathrm{Peyre}}B(\log B)^6. \] The argument starts from the universal-torsor parametrization and combines two counting methods over complementary ranges of the auxiliary variables. The two-dimensional lattice count is controlled by averages of reciprocal shortest-vector lengths and character-moment bounds, while Poisson summation treats the complementary parameter range. The main contribution is the uniform control needed to combine these methods when the size parameters of the auxiliary variables vary independently: the estimates retain every coprimality condition, the original height weight, and the full set of auxiliary tuples contributing to the geometric error. Divisibility estimates without an additional power of the height parameter control the sieve tail and justify removing the sieve after taking the height limit. We track the derivative losses and boundary contributions throughout the summation, and identify the common continuous main term with Peyre's constant by computing the effective-cone volume and the real and finite local densities.

title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials
abstract: Let $\varphi_d$ be the Chebyshev polynomial with $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$, and let $H_d$ be the hyperelliptic curve $y^2=\varphi_d(x)$. We determine all pairs $(d,p)$, with $p\nmid2d$ prime, for which $H_d$ is maximal over some finite field of characteristic $p$, together with all such fields. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$ only partial results were known. In this case, for odd $d$ we show that the Jacobian of $H_d$ is supersingular if and only if $H_d$ is maximal over a finite extension of $\mathbb{F}_p$, and that this happens precisely when $d=\ell^n$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod4$ prime and $p$ a generator of $(\mathbb{Z}/\ell^n\mathbb{Z})^\times$; we also compute the Frobenius polynomial. Necessity comes from the Shimura--Taniyama formula together with the non-vanishing of the value at $0$ of certain Dirichlet L-series and information about the action of Frobenius on $2$-torsion. The case of even $d$ and $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ follows from the odd case, by a short reduction.

title: Affine Springer fibers, Cherednik algebra modules and Hilbert schemes: torus link case
abstract: For a pair of positive integers $M,N$ with GCD $d$, we relate the bigraded $S_N\times S_d$-Frobenius characters of the homology of the positive part of a homogeneous affine Springer fiber for $\mathrm{GL}_N$ of slope $M/N$ to a direct sum of the associated graded of minimal supported modules of type $A_{N-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra at the same slope, and to the equivariant K-theory of a coherent sheaf on the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. For the first object, we use the Hessenberg paving of Goresky-Kottwitz-Macpherson; for the second and third objects, we resort to an explicit Hodge module on $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. The bridge between them is a non-coprime shuffle theorem of Kim-Oh.

title: Calabi-energy sublevels, K-stability and Calabi flow
abstract: In this paper, we prove path connectedness of every nonempty strict Calabi-energy sublevel and identify the infimum of the square root of the Calabi energy over smooth metrics with the infimum of the descending Mabuchi slope in the metric completion. In particular, there exist smooth metrics of arbitrarily small Calabi energy in every K-semistable real ample class. On compact Kähler surfaces, we prove the existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics in the K-polystable classes of the controlled cone. In any class containing such a metric, the Calabi flow exists smoothly for all time with a uniform Sobolev bound whenever the initial metric is smooth and has sufficiently small Calabi energy.

title: Coxeter cubes on the graph associahedron and separable elements
abstract: A Coxeter cube is a Boolean lattice inside a finite Coxeter group $W$ such that every square is a Coxeter square in the sense of Dyer and Wang. A Coxeter cube of full dimension based at the identity, which we call a based cube, is the same as a partition of the positive roots into inversion sets with one simple root in each block. These partitions were studied by Dimitrov, Gigliotti, Ossip, Paquette and Wehlau under the name of fine decompositions, and by Hohlweg and Pons as partitions of $w_0$. We show that the based cubes of $W$ form a point configuration in the graph associahedron $K(Γ)$ of the Coxeter diagram $Γ$ of $W$. The vertices of $K(Γ)$ are the based cubes whose blocks are parabolic. Every other based cube lies in the interior of an edge or of a cubical face, and we count the based cubes on each edge using the Coxeter arrangement. We also characterize the elements of $W$ that occur as vertices of based cubes. For the cubes at the vertices of $K(Γ)$ these are exactly the separable elements of Gaetz and Gao, and for arbitrary based cubes they satisfy a similar condition.

title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
abstract: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.

title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.

title: Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties via Symplectic Cuts
abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric orbifold of complex dimension $2n$ by compact symplectic cuts. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region and the fixed lift is integral, we prove that, at every positive regular integral level $d$, the space of sections on the cut is the sum of the fibre-rotation weight spaces of weight at most $d$ in the original quantisation. The higher cohomology of the cut pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes, so its equivariant index is the character of its actual section space. Using the moment polyptychs introduced in a companion paper, we give an orbifold Kawasaki-Riemann-Roch localisation formula for this character. We also compute it as a weighted lattice-point sum: a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if the arrangement slack function satisfies $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. The examples compare these calculations in rank one, including a cut with an orbifold point, and in rank two, for smooth cuts that are not toric.

title: Generalized Frobenius manifolds: symmetries and their classification in 2-dimensions
abstract: A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.

title: Random Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space
abstract: We introduce Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space as a weighted generalization of Voronoi tessellations and a hyperbolic analogue of Euclidean power diagrams. We present geometric and analytic constructions and establish conditions under which a collection of weighted points generates a well-defined tessellation. For Poisson point processes of weighted points, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the intensity measure ensuring that the resulting diagram is almost surely a tessellation. We then prove that hyperbolic Poisson-Laguerre tessellations are stable under intersections with totally geodesic subspaces, with an explicit transformation of the intensity measure. As applications, we identify the Poisson-Laguerre tessellations arising as sections of hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi and ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellations. In particular, the latter have unbounded cells, while their proper totally geodesic sections have bounded cells almost surely.

title: Triviality of metric fibrations over locally finite metric graphs
abstract: In this note, we give a direct proof that every metric fibration over a geodesic metric space locally modeled on finite metric stars is isometrically isomorphic, over its base, to the $\ell^1$ product of its base and a fiber. Neither compactness nor completeness of the base is assumed. We also construct a nontrivial example over a closed interval with a truncated metric, showing that the local star condition alone does not imply the conclusion.

title: Forecast Projection and Decision Regret: Theory and Evidence from Battery Arbitrage
abstract: Decision-focused learning trains forecasts for the decisions they lead to, but forecasts are often projected onto known bounds before use. We study the resulting mismatch in battery arbitrage. When a battery starts and ends the day at the same charge level, a common shift in prices affects its schedule only through round-trip losses. As a result, decision-focused losses identify the forecast level only weakly. For the SPO+ and perturbed Fenchel-Young losses, we characterize the preferred level by a throughput-matching condition. Projecting forecasts onto a price cap can then remove profitable spreads and increase regret, even as prediction error falls. We give bounds on the change in regret, a dual-threshold condition under which a raw-optimal schedule remains optimal after clipping, and a general version of the mechanism for other problems with a conservation constraint. On 1,158 holdout days of the Indian day-ahead market, an equal-weight average of three statistical forecasts outperforms the five decision-focused variants tested. On 53 later days, with 62% of price blocks at the cap, no variant outperforms the regression or the equal-weight average, although most differences from the average are not significant. The results suggest that forecast post-processing should be treated as part of the predict-then-optimize pipeline.

title: A linear programming approach to finite copula interpolation
abstract: We consider exact and interval-valued interpolation of multivariate copulas at arbitrary finite configurations in the unit cube. We first characterize when the prescribed data are compatible with a quasi-copula and derive explicit extremal quasi-copula envelopes. The copula interpolation problem is thereby reduced to a copula sandwich problem between these envelopes. Restricting them to the canonical rectangular grid generated by the data coordinates yields a finite linear feasibility system whose elementary-volume constraints are encoded by a cell--vertex incidence matrix. Farkas' lemma then identifies the criterion of Omladič and Stopar with an explicit certificate of infeasibility. Although this criterion is indexed by infinitely many formal cell combinations, we show that it suffices to test finitely many vertices of a sign-polytopal subdivision. We also extend the construction to $k$-increasing discrete quasi-copulas for $2\leq k\leq d$.

title: Frege's election method: discrepancy, invariant polygons and Farey geometry
abstract:
We give a comprehensive study of Frege's modified election method as a proportional allocation rule and as a dynamical system. The method was introduced by Harrenstein, Lackner and Lackner (2022) as a modification of Frege's original proposal (1918), and it coincides with the greedy algorithm for the chairman assignment problem studied by Coppersmith et al. (2011). We consider several aspects of this method.
  First, we prove that the harmonic bound on the discrepancy earlier shown to be sharp for time-dependent vote proportions remains sharp for fixed vote proportions; we further quantify the restrictions on votes needed for the discrepancy to come close to this bound.
  Secondly, the method defines a dynamical system with a piecewise translation which, for almost every vote vector, has a unique compact attractor made up of finitely many polytopes, and every orbit is equidistributed on it, whatever choices are made at ties.
  Thirdly, for three parties, the dynamics is two-dimensional. We construct the invariant polygons explicitly and give a complete description of the geometry governing their bifurcations as the votes vary in the two-dimensional parameter space; this space is partitioned into a countably infinite number of ``Farey cells'' indexed by reduced fractions in $(0,\frac12]$, and each of them is further partitioned into a finite number of stability domains, separated by stability walls. In an open Farey cell indexed by a reduced fraction $u/v$, the invariant polygon has $4v+3$ vertices inside each stability domain and $4v+2$ on an internal stability wall. We construct the Farey cells explicitly and determine all stability walls and their endpoints; we also show that stability walls in different Farey cells combine to form a pattern of triangles.

title: On $q$-Ary $t$-Designs from Codewords of Every Nonzero Weight in Linear Codes and Their Duals
abstract: The paper investigates when the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design and how to generalize the property to its dual code. We reduce the verification of this property to a prescribed range of low weights. Specifically, for MDS codes, we show that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at every nonzero weight is equivalent to that at any fixed nonzero weight. As an application, we prove that the codewords of every nonzero weight in a $[q+1,3,q-1]_q$ MDS code and its dual hold $q$-ary $2$-designs if and only if $q$ is even. We also establish a duality principle. When $t\le\min\{d,d^{\perp}\}$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design if and only if the same property holds for its dual code. We then investigate narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,δ,1)}$ and their duals. For $q=2^m$ and $δ=2^r$ with $1\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in these codes form $q$-ary $2$-designs. Furthermore, for $δ=4$ and $q=2^{m}$ ($m\ge4$), we establish that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,4,1)}$ form a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $m$ is odd.

title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
abstract: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.

title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
abstract: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.

title: Asymptotic Bayes Optimality of Sparse Multiple Testing Procedures under One-Factor Dependence
abstract: In this paper, we study sparse multiple testing under a Gaussian two-group model with known one-factor covariance and centered Gaussian signals. We derive a first-order risk expansion for the observed-data Bayes Oracle, including a finite-dimensional loading average for heterogeneous loadings and an explicit limiting constant for homogeneous loadings. Under the stated factor-estimation and signal-calibration conditions, the homogeneous one-factor Oracle has strictly smaller leading risk than its independent-coordinate counterpart; observing the latent factor yields no further first-order reduction. We establish asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity (ABOS) for the Maximum Residual Down (MRD) step-down procedure with Gavrilov--Benjamini--Sarkar (GBS) stagewise calibration (MRD--GBS). Uniform control of residual errors along the rejection path permits comparison with a fixed factor-known rule without requiring the rejection paths to coincide. Fixed-residual versions of GBS and Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) attain the same leading risk. We also prove ABOS for the Bayesian Step-Down (BSD) rule when supplied with the true mixture, signal variance, covariance, and loss parameters; this is an Oracle-parameterized result. When the expected signal count grows faster than the logarithm of the reciprocal signal proportion, BSD and the observed-data Oracle disagree on several coordinates negligible in probability relative to the expected signal count, explaining BSD's near-Oracle behavior in companion simulations. The results cover diverging and bounded positive expected signal counts, including every fixed polynomial sparsity rate up to the bounded-count regime, under the stated calibrations. A fixed-dimension simulation illustrates absolute-risk behavior but does not establish ABOS.

title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions
abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(Γ, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.

title: Pólya's conjecture for hyperbolic balls and Berezin--Li--Yau type inequalities
abstract:
We prove the strict shifted Dirichlet Pólya inequality \[ λ_k(B_R)>\frac{(d-1)^2κ^2}{4}+4π^2\left(\frac{k}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(B_R)}\right)^{2/d},\qquad k\ge1, \] for every geodesic ball $B_R$ in hyperbolic space of constant sectional curvature $-κ^2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$. As a consequence, we obtain the shifted Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality for hyperbolic balls, thereby providing a concrete family of domains satisfying both conjectures proposed by Laptev in 2023.
  For arbitrary nonempty open subsets $Ω\subset\mathbb{H}^d_κ$ of finite volume, we establish the weak Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}λ_j(Ω)\ge a_{d,κ}m+\frac{d}{d+2}\,4π^2\left(\frac{m}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(Ω)}\right)^{2/d}m,\qquad m\ge1, \] with the optimal leading coefficient, where $a_{2,κ}=κ^2/4$ and $a_{d,κ}=d(d-1)κ^2/6$ for $d\ge3$. We also establish the global two-sided estimate for the renormalized eigenvalue sum on hyperbolic space, originally proposed by Strichartz in 1996 and valid for $d\ge3$.

title: The Role of Insurance in Power-System Risk Management: A Critical Review
abstract: Modern power systems are becoming more renewable-rich, digitalized, and interconnected, making risk propagation and economic consequences increasingly complex. Physical mitigation remains the primary means of risk control, but technical and economic limits leave residual risk. Insurance can complement these measures by transferring associated economic losses and influencing power-system decisions through risk-responsive terms. Despite growing interest, the literature remains fragmented across power-system engineering, actuarial science, and risk finance. This review develops an integrated physical-financial perspective for reviewing insurance in power systems. It examines how power system risks generate residual economic losses and the conditions under which these losses can be insured and transferred. It then develops an actuarial framework for insured-loss assessment and pricing. Insurance-aware decision-making is synthesized through four coupling levels describing how financial protection interacts with power-system decisions. Further progress is constrained by weak physical-financial loss validation, incomplete representation of systemic and evolving portfolio risk, and limited empirical and actuarial grounding of insurance-decision feedback. Research priorities include stronger physical-financial data linkage, forward-looking portfolio assessment, multi-timescale decision feedback, and empirical validation. Addressing these priorities would help move power-system insurance from fragmented applications toward a more coherent approach to residual-risk management in future power systems.

title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_σ$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $σ$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $Ω=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a Hölder Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $μ\in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (μ)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $σ$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(μ)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(μ)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_σ$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:Ω\to \mathbb{R}$. $μ\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(ρ|| ν)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.

title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
abstract: Let $γ$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_γ$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,δ)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$.

title: Monotone Rearrangement for Flattening Weights $F_2$
abstract: We consider a subclass of the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ weights with added smoothness, which we refer to as flattening weights $F_2.$ We quantify how such weights arise as exponents of VMO functions and prove that monotone rearrangement does not increase the class modulus in $F_2.$

title: Uniqueness of global weak solutions for the defocusing energy-critical NLS
abstract: We study the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation and establish global uniqueness for weak solutions. The key idea comes from the weak uniqueness in the uniform-in-time high-frequency threshold (UTHT) class introduced in [12,14]. We derive a new energy defect threshold (EDT) criterion from the UTHT criterion. Along the strong solution flow, energy conservation propagates the EDT condition for weak solutions and, combined with the global well-posedness theory for strong solutions, yields global weak uniqueness. As an application, we prove unconditional uniqueness for the quintic defocusing energy-critical Gross-Pitaevskii hierarchy.

title: A Strategic Freight Market Model for Liner Shipping: Pricing, Entry, and Endogenous Service Choice
abstract: National freight transport models usually treat prices and service provision as exogenous. This paper models both as outcomes of strategic interaction among operators of scheduled, loop-based freight services. It compares oligopolistic competition, monopoly, Ramsey pricing with service-level or system-wide cost recovery, and welfare-maximising planning. Shippers across multiple segments choose between direct cyclic liner services and an outside option, using logit demand. Operators select from candidate port rotations, vessel classes and speeds, and set origin-destination prices subject to leg capacities. Under competition, each operator offers one service. Equilibrium requires that no operator can profitably enter, exit or replace its service after prices re-equilibrate. The solution method computes global pricing best responses and tests all unilateral service deviations, pruning only those excluded by an analytical profit bound. All regimes use the same demand and cost structure. In a synthetic Baltic-North Sea application, multinomial logit competition sustains more overlapping services and lower prices than monopoly. System-wide Ramsey pricing captures most of the planner's welfare gain without a deficit. Fuel-price and demand shocks affect competitive prices through changes in the service set. When maritime services are close substitutes, entrants avoid overlapping markets and competition can reproduce monopoly outcomes. The results illustrate mechanisms rather than forecast actual markets, showing how market organisation shapes service provision, prices, modal shares and welfare.

title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests and complete bipartite graphs
abstract: For a graph $G$ and an integer $m\ge2$ dividing $e(G)$, where $e(G)$ denotes the number of edges of $G$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb Z_m)$ is the least $N$ such that every $\mathbb Z_m$-labeling of $E(K_N)$ contains a copy of $G$ whose edge labels sum to zero. Bialostocki and Dierker (1990) [4] conjectured that $R(F,\mathbb Z_{e(F)})/R(F,2)\to1$ uniformly over all forests $F$ as $e(F)\to\infty$, where $R(F,2)$ is the two-color Ramsey number, and Caro (1991) [9] conjectured that $R(tG,\mathbb Z_t)=t(|V(G)|+d)-d$ for $t\ge2$ disjoint copies of $G$, where $d=\operatorname{def}_t(G)$ is the defect. We disprove the first conjecture by an infinite family of trees. Building on the work of Caro and on his joint work with Provstgaard, we obtain infinitely many counterexamples to the second conjecture, and we determine the zero-sum Ramsey numbers of a class of graphs: for powers of two $q\ge2$ we characterize all $s,k\ge1$ satisfying $R(K_{s,kq},\mathbb Z_q)=s+kq$, and we prove $R(mK_{q,q},\mathbb Z_m)=2qm+m/\gcd(m,q)-1$ for every $m\ge2$.

title: Linear circle quotients of products of odd-dimensional spheres: classification and geometric applications
abstract: In this paper, we study the orbit manifolds of free diagonal linear circle actions on \(S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\). For every \(n\geq 1\), we establish a PL homeomorphism classification of the orbit manifolds in terms of the weights of the actions. We also obtain diffeomorphism classification and homotopy classification of such orbit manifolds in dimension $9$ and $13$. The diffeomorphism classification results lead to two geometric applications. For every \(m\geq 1\), there exist a non-spin \(9\)-manifold \(M_m^9\) and a spin \(13\)-manifold \(M_m^{13}\) in our family such that the moduli space of unit-volume homogeneous Einstein metrics on each manifold has at least \(2^{m-1}\) connected components. Moreover, each of these manifolds admits at least \(2^{m-1}\) regular Sasakian structures whose underlying contact structures are pairwise non-contactomorphic.

title: Integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points in the Heisenberg group
abstract: We investigate the local integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points of surfaces in the first Heisenberg group. We prove that, for every embedded surface of class $C^{2,α}$, with $α>0$, the horizontal mean curvature is locally integrable with respect to (any) Riemannian surface measure, without any assumption on the structure of the characteristic set. We further establish that the horizontal unit normal belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and characterize its $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity in terms of the vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the characteristic set. Finally, we answer an open question by Danielli, Garofalo and Nhieu by constructing a $C^2$ surface with a unique characteristic point whose horizontal mean curvature fails to be locally integrable, thus showing that the additional Hölder regularity cannot, in general, be replaced by $C^2$ regularity.

title: Numerical investigation of a MST conjecture for random Haar matrices
abstract: The state-to-state control time of finite-dimensional conservative bilinear quantum systems is bounded by the weight of minimum spanning trees (MST) derived from the drift matrices. For a spectrum scaling as k^3/2 , determining whether the control time vanishes as the dimension d tends to infinity remains an open problem due to the global correlations imposed by the Haar measure. We formulate two conjectures regarding the asymptotic behavior of the MST weight\,: a general decay to zero, and a scaling in 1/sqrt(ln d) derived from an independent Gaussian surrogate model. Numerical investigations up to dimension d = 18101 validate the general decay, confirm that the exact Haar model and the independent surrogate are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and extract the thermodynamic limit $α$ = 10/3, which both models approach from below once the scaling variable 1/ ln d is adopted.

title: Classical Tensor Codes and Quantum Tanner Codes Achieve Capacity on Erasure Channels
abstract: We show that on the classical erasure channel, the tensor product of two capacity-achieving code families is itself capacity-achieving under mild conditions. We also prove that duals of tensor products of independent uniform random binary linear codes achieve erasure capacity. Using these local codes, for every erasure probability $ρ\in(0,1/2)$ and every rate gap $\varepsilon>0$, we obtain a family of binary quantum Tanner codes of rate at least $1-2ρ-\varepsilon$. For fixed $ρ$ and $\varepsilon$, these codes have bounded check weights, minimum distance growing linearly with the blocklength, and a linear-time erasure decoder whose decoding error decays exponentially with the blocklength.

title: Treewidth versus Hadwiger number: Graph classes with dominated balanced separators are quasi-linearly treewidth-Hadwiger bounded
abstract: In a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, the treewidth of a graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is bounded by a function of the size of a largest clique minor of the graph if and only if the class $\mathcal{G}$ excludes some planar graph as an induced minor. Campbell et al. (arXiv 2024) conjectured that such a bounding function can always be chosen to be linear. We verify this conjecture for several classes of graphs (including even-hole-free graphs) and show that if a hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$ has dominated binary-weighted balanced separators, then the bounding function can be taken to be in ${O(h \log h)}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number. We say that $\mathcal{G}$ has dominated binary-weighted balanced separators if, for every ${G \in \mathcal{G}}$ and every $\mathsf{w} \colon V(G) \to \{0,1\}$, there is a set ${D \subseteq V(G)}$ of bounded size so that deleting the closed neighbourhood $N_G[D]$ of $D$ leaves each component with at most a fixed fraction of the total weight of $G$. Our result reduces the quasi-linear weakening of the conjecture of Campbell et al. to a conjecture of Gartland and Lokshtanov stating that every graph class excluding a planar graph as an induced minor admits dominated binary-weighted balanced separators.

title: Dual-Space Preconditioning for Variational Inequalities and Root-Finding Problems
abstract: This paper develops a dual-space preconditioning framework for variational inequalities and root-finding problems beyond classical cocoercivity and Lipschitz continuity assumptions. To this end, we introduce both a novel cocoercivity-type condition and a relaxed Lipschitz continuity condition, and derive convergence of deterministic and stochastic methods under these generalized conditions. For isotropic preconditioners, the resulting algorithms can be interpreted as variable-stepsize variants of classical methods, extending recent analyses based on $(L_0, L_1)$-type growth conditions while allowing simpler proofs and larger stepsize ranges. We also show that the framework naturally handles variational inequalities through weak Minty-type arguments. Finally, we study the associated continuous-time dynamics and derive a variational and optimal control interpretation of the preconditioned flow. Overall, the results show that dual-space preconditioning provides a flexible mechanism for designing and analyzing operator methods beyond the standard Euclidean Lipschitz setting.

title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
abstract: On bounded domains, the mass-conserving parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system admits smooth equilibria at every mass. Nevertheless, we prove that on a disk, an open dense set of positive initial densities leads to finite-time blow-up or infinite-time grow-up whenever the effective mass is at least the critical value $4π$. This threshold is sharp: below $4π$, every solution exists globally, remains uniformly bounded, and converges to a smooth equilibrium. At the critical mass, all solutions are global, while infinite-time grow-up accompanied by boundary concentration is generic. We extend the result to other bounded planar domains and closed surfaces, obtaining sharp mass thresholds for the round sphere and the flat square torus.

title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
abstract: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction. Second, we refute their log-concavity Conjecture 1: the same gap example violates log-concavity, and a further single-curve computation gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, which also fails log-concavity. Third, we establish the skew-shape block-statistic identity proposed in Kahane's Conjecture 4.4 (arXiv:2607.11225v1) for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, under an explicitly specified root-exclusion convention. Its proof combines commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations; the corresponding mathematical statements have Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. Fourth, we derive a bivariate block refinement whose coefficients are nonnegative after shifting the order parameter by one and, when necessary, multiplying by a monomial in the weight parameter. We specify the correction to the printed root convention, confirmed by Kahane in correspondence, and the geometric sign and specialization conventions clarified by the relevant authors for the annular examples.

title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
abstract: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the lifted invariants modulo every power of $p$. We also study isogenies between the zeros. Each $p$-power isogeny class contains at most one zero $j$-invariant, and any two distinct isogenous zero invariants are algebraic over $\mathbf{Q}$. At a fixed cyclic degree, the nonelliptic isogenies give points in a finite divisor over $\mathbf{Q}$ on the corresponding modular curve. Its degree bounds their number and their fields of definition, and excludes several small degrees. The only zeros with complex multiplication have $j=0$ or $1728$. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic $j$-invariant remains open.

title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
abstract: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.

title: A fourth-order dimensionally split exponential time differencing scheme with real and distinct pole rational approximation for non-linear reaction-diffusion systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel fourth-order, L-stable exponential time differencing (ETD) Runge-Kutta type scheme incorporating a dimensional splitting integrating factor method for the numerical solution of nonlinear reaction-diffusion systems.
